human_tolerance.notes: "Due to having a habit of eating human garbage in urban environments, raccoons are also colloquially known as 'trash pandas'." They use attic space as dens, raid fruit trees and overturn waste containers, and their range expansion into cities has been driven by urbanization, the expansion of agriculture, deliberate introductions and the extermination of their natural predators. Hunting and vehicular injury are the two most common causes of death.

phases.name: mating
phases.note: Mating is triggered by increasing daylight between late January and mid-March, though there are large regional differences not fully explicable by solar conditions: southern states mate later than average and Manitoba peaks later still, in March, extending to June.

phases.name: young
phases.note: Gestation is usually 63-65 days, with 54-70 possible; a litter is typically two to five kits, with average litter size ranging from 2.5 in Alabama to 4.8 in North Dakota. The mother raises the kits alone until dispersal in late fall; they are about eight weeks old before they would normally leave the nesting place, and mothers isolate themselves from other raccoons until the kits can defend themselves.

phases.name: dormancy
phases.note: "In the northern parts of their range, raccoons go into a winter rest, reducing their activity drastically as long as a permanent snow cover makes searching for food difficult." This is a reduction in activity driven by snow cover, not physiological torpor: an urban raccoon in a Michigan winter keeps feeding through it, which is why the record's strategy is ActiveYearRound.

vocalizations.description: The birdlike twittering of newborn kits, one of seven of the thirteen identified vocal calls that are used in communication between a mother and her kits. The record carries only this one call because the source names and describes only this one; inventing descriptions for the other twelve would not be honest.

external.note: NCBI taxon id via Wikidata P685.

common_names.note: The article gives common raccoon, North American raccoon and northern raccoon; the record uses common raccoon.

conservation.note: Wikidata P141 = least concern (Q211005). The three Caribbean island raccoons the article discusses were separate species and are not this record.

range.note: Common throughout North America from Canada to Panama; populations on Hispaniola, Cuba and Jamaica were hunted to extirpation and the Barbados raccoon went extinct in 1964, which is why no Caribbean codes are listed. Since the mid-20th century escapes and deliberate introductions have spread it across central Europe, the Caucasus and Japan; it has been on the EU list of Invasive Alien Species of Union concern since 2016, so invasive_in carries EU as one code for that list rather than inventing member-state entries. The article names Germany and the former Soviet Union explicitly, which are the introduced codes recorded.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: "As raccoons have short legs compared to their compact torso, they are usually not able to run quickly or jump great distances" - a top speed of 16-24 km/h over short distances - but they climb by rotating the hind feet to come down a tree headfirst, and they 'can swim with an average speed of about 5 km/h and can stay in the water for several hours'.

traits.nest_type.note: "Tree hollows in old oaks or other trees and rock crevices are preferred by raccoons as sleeping, winter, and litter dens", with burrows dug by other mammals, dense undergrowth or tree crotches used when those are unavailable; the urban equivalent is attic space.

traits.perching.note: Climbs and climbs down headfirst by rotating its hind feet, but does not perch on a branch the way a bird does; set to false, matching the treatment of the other rodents in this repository.

traits.senses.note: "The most important sense for the raccoon is its sense of touch", with almost two-thirds of its sensory cortex devoted to it, which is what vibration records. "With their broad auditory range, they can perceive tones up to 50-85 kHz as well as quiet noises, like those produced by earthworms underground." Scent-marking with anal-gland secretions, urine and faeces is the olfactory channel.

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits MamFuncDat BodyMass-Value 5524.97 g, which falls at the bottom of Wikipedia's 'usually between 5 and 12 kg' band.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: The article's usual 5-12 kg band, not its 2-26 kg extremes: smallest specimens are in southern Florida and the largest are near the northern limit of the range, and at the beginning of winter a raccoon can weigh twice its spring mass. Males are 15-20% heavier than females. The record specimen is 28.4 kg.

traits.length_m.note: The schema wants nose to tail tip and the article gives the two parts separately: head to hindquarters 40-70 cm (mid 55 cm) and a bushy tail of 20-40 cm that is 'usually not much longer than 25 cm'. Adding the mid body length to the usual tail gives about 80 cm. The record specimen's total length of 140 cm is the extreme.

traits.shoulder_height_m.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia's 23-30 cm shoulder height.

traits.lifespan_y.note: "Although captive raccoons have been known to live over 20 years, their life expectancy in the wild is only 1.8 to 3.1 years." The schema asks for the wild figure, so the midpoint of that range is used. Hunting and vehicular injury are the two most common causes of death.

traits.home_range_ha.note: Taken as the city figure, since this record supports a suburban plot: the article gives 3 ha for females in cities and up to 5,000 ha for males in prairies, and says adults claim areas more than twice as large as juveniles. A single number cannot carry that range, so the small end relevant to the locale is used and the full span is recorded here.

traits.diet.note: The article's own fractions are used: 'about 40% invertebrates, 33% plant material and 27% vertebrates'. The plant third is split as mast 0.20 and fruit 0.13 because the article says it prefers fruits and nuts such as acorns and walnuts, without a finer breakdown. EltonTraits independently gives Diet-Inv 40, Diet-Seed 20, Diet-Fruit 20 and Diet-Vect 20, which agrees on the invertebrate share and the same order of magnitude elsewhere.

traits.social.note: "Related females often live in a so-called 'fission-fusion society'; that is, they share a common area and occasionally meet at feeding or resting grounds. Unrelated males often form loose male social groups ... Such a group does not usually consist of more than four individuals." Zeveloff is more cautious and concludes females are solitary most of the time; the record takes Group with a ceiling of 4, the one hard number the article gives.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits Activity-Nocturnal 1 with Diurnal and Crepuscular 0, and the article's 'It is usually nocturnal and omnivorous' agree. It 'is sometimes active in daylight to take advantage of available food sources'.

traits.defense.note: Flee: 'raccoons depend on vertical structures to climb when they feel threatened', which is why it avoids open terrain and beech woods with too-smooth bark. Cornered raccoons bite viciously and killings of people and pets are reported, but the schema has no bite response and flight up a tree is the documented first move. The mask is also said to reduce glare and enhance night vision.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: 0.3. Bold - it denns in attics, raids fruit trees and overturns bins in settled areas, and studies show it can remember the solution to tasks for at least three years - but it relies on climbing to escape a threat and mothers with small kits keep well clear of other raccoons.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat-Value 'G' gives the ground stratum as primary, which fits an animal that forages through leaf litter, refuses to cross open terrain without a climbable structure within reach, and only dabbles at the water's edge; the arboreal share covers the head-first tree descent and denning, and no source quantifies the split.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet exactly. water is recorded because it 'often dabble[s] for underwater food near the shoreline' and because amphibians and crustaceans around lake and river shores are an important part of the diet. Nesting weight is entirely on the tree hollow or crevice; burrow and leaf_litter carry the fallback dens and the dense undergrowth the habitat section names, and are weighted by judgement.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: The notes field quotes the 'trash pandas' line and records the rest of the evidence: range expansion into urban areas driven by urbanization and agriculture, attic denning, raiding fruit trees and bins, and hunting plus vehicular injury as the two commonest causes of death. impervious_max, dist_building_min_m, flight_distance_m and road_mortality are authored judgement on that description and are not quantified in the source; dist_building_min_m is 0 because denning in attics puts it inside the building.

habitat.density_per_ha.note: Judgement: the article gives no density, only that the North American population was 15 to 20 times higher by the late 1980s than in the 1930s, and that lowland deciduous or mixed forest abundant with water and marshes sustains the highest densities. Home ranges of about 3 ha for city females give typical 0.3 per hectare, and min and max are an authored tenfold band either side, following the convention used for turdus-migratorius and sciurus-carolinensis.

seasonal.strategy.note: ActiveYearRound, deliberately rather than Torpor: the article describes a 'winter rest' in the northern part of the range that reduces activity 'as long as a permanent snow cover makes searching for food difficult', which is a snow-driven reduction in foraging rather than a physiological state, and an urban raccoon in a Michigan lot keeps feeding through winter. The behaviour is recorded as a dormancy phase instead, with that reasoning stated there.

seasonal.phases.note: The late-January to mid-March daylight-triggered mating season with its regional variation, the 63-65 day gestation and 54-70 day full range, the typical litter of two to five and the 2.5 to 4.8 average-litter range across Alabama and North Dakota, maternal-only rearing to dispersal in late fall, the kits' eight weeks in the nesting place, the mother isolating herself until the kits can defend themselves, and the northern winter rest are all stated in the article.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Juvenile duration is authored: kits are born in spring after about 65 days' gestation and are raised by the mother 'until dispersal in late fall', about seven months. scale is authored judgement.

vocalizations.note: The single recorded call is the birdlike twittering of newborns, and the note above the source's caveat that it is one of seven of thirteen identified calls used between a mother and her kits. The article does not name or describe the other twelve, so they are not invented here; the months and the Night window follow the spring-to-late-fall rearing season, and the cooldown is authored judgement. No open source gives frequency bands, so freq_hz is omitted.

look.note: Colours from the Physical characteristics and lead paragraphs: a grayish coat of dense underfur with long stiff guard hairs in shades of gray and, to a lesser extent, brown; the black fur around the eyes forming the 'bandit's mask' against a sharply contrasting white face; slightly rounded ears bordered by white fur; and alternating light and dark rings on the tail. The mask part renders the bandit's mask and the tail band renders the rings. Proportions are authored judgement for a compact, short-legged, ring-tailed procyonid; the quadruped body plan has no neck part, so nothing is parented to one. No open source describes the eye colour, so eye is a judgement value.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared ground-forager program. food_tag is invertebrate because that is the single largest sourced diet share and what it finds by rummaging through leaf litter; rest_sun_lo_deg and rest_sun_hi_deg are deliberately left at the program's own defaults of 10 and 90, which rest the animal while the sun is up - correct for a nocturnal species, and the opposite of what sciurus-niger needs; flee_m 15 m, calm_m 40 m and food_m 40 m sit between the fox defaults and the squirrel values for an animal of this size and boldness, with flee_gait gallop for the sprint to the nearest climbable structure.
